name: Djibouti
subtitle: Djibouti, capital of Djibouti: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: France established a base at Obock on the north shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura in 1862, bought from the sultan of Tadjoura; the administrative centre was later moved to Djibouti.
The year 1888 marked the decline of Obock and the birth of Djibouti as a bridgehead between north-east Africa and Arabia.

parts.text: France established a base at Obock on the north shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura in 1862, bought from the sultan of Tadjoura; the administrative centre was later moved to Djibouti.
The year 1888 marked the decline of Obock and the birth of Djibouti as a bridgehead between north-east Africa and Arabia.

Site choice: Governor Lagarde judged the Obock roadstead too narrow and unsafe and chose Ras Djibouti for its large sheltered roadstead and access to the Ethiopian plateaus; the government moved there in 1892.

Djibouti became capital of the Côte française des Somalis in 1896 (Lagarde moved the seat there in 1894, per Universalis); the town grew with the railway to Addis Ababa built 1897-1917. Note: Douteau gives 1892 for the move, Universalis 1894; sources differ.
The territory was renamed Territoire français des Afars et des Issas in July 1967; independence was set for 27 June 1977 after a May 1977 referendum.
The port developed first as a coaling station and then as a railhead for trains from Ethiopia; the city handles most of East Africa's trade through its seaport (EBSCO).

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Djibouti?

parts.text: 767,250 in 2024, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Census population (census date 2024-05-20) of the city 'Djibouti (Djibouti-Ville)' as a sum of three communes (Balbala, Boulaos, Ras Dika); no formal boundary definition given on the page.

items.text: France holds the territory of Obock, bought from the sultan of Tadjoura.
Obock declines and Djibouti is born as a bridgehead between north-east Africa and Arabia.
The colonial government moves to Ras Djibouti (date per Douteau; Universalis gives 1894 for the transfer).
Djibouti becomes capital of the Côte française des Somalis.
Construction of the railway to Addis Ababa begins (growth of the city tied to it, 1897-1917).
The territory is renamed Territoire français des Afars et des Issas.
Independence of the Republic of Djibouti.
